chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the vessel in which wine has been, whether it is permissible for vinegar, kamakh water, or olives to be placed in it? He said: 'If it is washed, there is no harm.'
And about the ewer and other vessels in which wine has been, whether it is permissible for water to be placed in it? He said: 'If it is washed, there is no harm.'
And he said regarding a cup or vessel from which wine is drunk: 'He should wash it three times.'
He was asked: 'Is it sufficient for him to pour water into it?' He said: 'It is not sufficient until he rubs it with his hand and washes it three times.'

key_terms.الْخَمْرُ: Wine (specifically the intoxicant, often used as the category for najasah)
key_terms.مَاءُ كَامَخٍ: Kamakh water (a type of fruit juice/drink)

ai.seo_question: How many times must a wine vessel be washed to become pure in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *istihlak* (purification) for vessels contaminated by wine (*khamr*), distinguishing between general containers and specific drinking vessels. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that while general washing suffices for most items, drinking vessels require manual rubbing (*dalak*) and three rinsings to ensure complete removal of the wine's essence, reflecting the Shia emphasis on tactile cleanliness in ritual purity.
